story.title: The New York Times reportedly in talks to buy Letterboxd for $330 million

facts.text: The company that owns The New York Times is in "exclusive negotiations" to purchase the cinephile online platform Letterboxd, anonymous sources told...
The price being discussed is reportedly around $330 million, significantly more than the $250 million figure that was bandied around earlier this year .
Discussions are ongoing and could still break down, the report states.
Letterboxd would reportedly continue operations as a standalone site for the "foreseeable future," the NYT reported.
The Times Company also has a similar business model with a mix of ad and subscription revenue.
Though relatively small with 30 million members, Letterboxd is an influential online film site with a dedicated and active community that includes notable figures like Martin Scorsese .
Brace yourselves, cinephiles: the place where you log every movie you watch, rank your favorites, and passive-aggressively rate your friends' picks might be getting a new owner.
According to a New York Times report, the Times Company is in exclusive negotiations to acquire Letterboxd.
The reported price tag is around $330 million.
If you've ever spiraled into a 2 a.m. rabbit hole of other people's hyper-specific Letterboxd lists, you already know why this is a big deal.
The site has become the hangout for movie obsessives, with a reported 30 million users reviewing films, building hyper-specific lists, and taking on viewing challenges.
Letterboxd's value rests on something no acquisition price can guarantee: the trust of 30 million people who treat it as their own corner of the internet.
The Times has a record of buying beloved properties and folding them into a bundle , and promises of independence tend to be tested after the deal closes, not before.
Nothing is signed, and neither side has commented publicly.
But if the talks succeed, the question won't be whether the Times can afford Letterboxd.
That's a hefty premium for a site that mostly runs on people's love of rewatching Challengers and cooking up one-liners they can then post on X.
But Letterboxd runs on both subscriptions and ads, just like the Times, and that overlap is clearly part of the appeal.
The Times currently has 13.8 million subscribers and wants to hit 15 million by the end of 2027.
Letterboxd doesn't say how many people pay for its premium tiers, but a loyal, paying fan base is just what that target needs.
The sources are anonymous since the talks are confidential, so nothing is final.
But exclusive negotiations are a pretty big step past "we're just looking."
Letterboxd would add a whole new pocket of passionate, extremely online fans to that lineup.
Letterboxd, which launched in 2011, has reportedly been working with investment bank LionTree to find a buyer, and the guest list for this party was stacked.
Film studios A24 and Sony were both reportedly interested.

A24 even pledged to give the founders independence and leave the business model alone, which sounds like exactly what you'd want to hear if you were nervous about a studio buying the site where people review its movies.
But the price kept climbing, and A24 reportedly got priced out.
Letterboxd would likely keep running as its own standalone site for the foreseeable future, though the Times reportedly plans to plug its ad tech into the platform.
The New York Times Company has reportedly “entered exclusive negotiations” to acquire Letterboxd for $330 million, according to a report from The New York Times itself.
Letterboxd is free, but users can access advanced features with a paid subscription.
Its projected earnings for this year are estimated at $15 million, which is only about 4.5% of what the Times is supposedly offering to buy the company for.
Personally, we wouldn’t be surprised if these anonymous tips were coming from inside the house, so we’re inclined to take this report pretty seriously.
Letterboxd, an online platform for movie lovers that could be compared to Goodreads for movies, has grown dramatically in recent years.
Letterboxd reported 3 million users in January 2021, a figure that grew to 28 million by April of this year.
Letterboxd was previously reported to be seeking a new owner.
According to the Times, film studios A24 and Sony were interested in the acquisition, but A24 was priced out.
The New York Times Company has reportedly entered exclusive negotiations to acquire the film enthusiasts’ platform Letterboxd for $330 million.
The company declined to comment on the possible deal.
Letterboxd can be used free of charge, while advanced features are available through a paid subscription.
It was previously reported that Letterboxd was looking for a new owner.
Letterboxd is an online platform for film fans, compared to Goodreads for movies.
Its number of users grew from 3 million in January 2021 to 28 million in April this year.
More than half of the service’s audience is under 35.
